title: Embedded <object> content needs alternative text
summary: An <object> element has no accessible name, so assistive technology cannot say what it holds. Add an aria-label, title or fallback text.
problem: An <object> element embeds an external file such as an SVG, PDF or other media, but it has no aria-label, aria-labeledby or title attribute, and no text inside it. Assistive technology cannot say what the embedded item is.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users meet an unnamed embedded item and cannot tell whether it is a chart, a map or an advertisement, so they cannot decide whether to explore it or skip it.
steps: Find <object> elements in your templates. The scan result shows the exact markup.
Add an aria-label that says what the embedded item is, such as aria-label="Sales by month, bar chart".
You can instead add a title attribute, or put fallback text inside the <object> element.
If the file has a text equivalent, such as a data table, place it near the object.
after: <object data="/files/sales-chart.svg" type="image/svg+xml" width="400" height="300" aria-label="Sales by month, bar chart"></object>
whyItMatters: Embedded content that carries information needs a text alternative under WCAG 1.1.1, a Level A criterion. An unnamed chart or document hides its content from people who cannot see it.
howToCheck: Open the browser accessibility inspector, select the <object> element and read its Name. An empty Name means no alternative text is present.
